Measured: E001 (9 ep) acc 0.7430, 9.43 s; E002 (10 ep) acc 0.7495, 10.55 s; both complete, both infeasible (<0.753). Each ran 3 seeds only.

1. Epoch dial (E001→E002, measured): +0.65 pp per epoch and +1.11 s per epoch (about 11.8% time per epoch). Fixed cost is therefore about 9.43 − 9×1.11 ≈ −0.5 s, which is within noise. That suggests nearly all time scales with epochs and fixed costs (data move, eigh, augment) are small, under 0.5 s. This weakens H3's claim that fixed costs are over 10%. Extrapolating, 0.753 needs about 10.5 to 10.7 epochs, which is about 11.1 to 11.3 s. The slope is probably concave, so I'd budget 11 epochs (~11.7 s) for a safe margin. My previous round's accuracy point forecast was 0.752 against 0.7495 measured, so I was slightly optimistic and the slope was a bit lower than I assumed.

2. Time per epoch is about 1.1 s, which is eager-bound, and that makes systems work the main lever for any fixed epoch count. A 10 to 15% gain from compile, fused SGD and a cheaper augment (the 25-way masked copy loop) is plausible but unmeasured here. Each percent saved on time converts to roughly 0.1 epoch, which buys about 0.07 pp.

3. Accuracy-side tricks (EMA/Lookahead, LS, flip) are unmeasured. Whatever gives +0.65 pp is worth one epoch, about 1.1 s, which is 10%. EMA at a +0.2 to 0.4 pp gain would be worth about 0.3 to 0.6 epochs. Muon and progressive resizing are risky because they change the training dynamics at a tuned lr/schedule, so I expect accuracy loss.

4. Noise: not directly measured. The step from 9 to 10 epochs is a clean +0.65 pp, consistent with the assumed 3-seed-mean std of about 0.15 to 0.25 pp. Time noise is assumed 1 to 2%. I005 will calibrate this. The sampling noise level means 0.753 on 3 seeds is itself uncertain by about ±0.2 pp, so sitting just above the bar risks failing the 40-seed judgment.

Unsure: whether compile actually helps with 4 CPU cores and with eval shapes included, whether the slope stays at 0.65 pp/epoch beyond 10 epochs, and whether EMA gives at least 0.2 pp.

forecasts.reason: Eager is launch-bound at about 1.1 s/epoch; compile plus fused SGD likely trims 10 to 15% with the same math, though autotune and eval-shape risks remain.
Late-training EMA typically adds 0.2 to 0.4 pp in short schedules at a small time cost, but it is unmeasured here and the gain is close to the noise.
A rerun should land near E002; the seeds are the same, so accuracy drift only comes from GPU nondeterminism, and time drift is about 1 to 2%.
The loop already uses n//bs and drops the ragged batch, so the shape is already uniform and the gain over the compiled port is near zero, below the 0.3 s claim.
Muon with an untuned lr and batch 2000 means fewer steps and extra Newton-Schulz cost; I expect lower accuracy and no time win at this budget.
Low resolution saves about 10% of FLOPs but the loss of about 0.5 pp costs about 0.8 epoch (about 9% time), so the net is roughly neutral and likely still infeasible.

cruxes: How much per-step time does torch.compile plus fused SGD actually save under the 4-CPU pin, and does the eval path stay under 5 s?
Does the accuracy slope stay near 0.65 pp/epoch past 10 epochs, and what is the real per-seed std (I005)?
Does EMA/Lookahead add at least 0.3 pp at fixed epochs, enough to replace about 0.5 epoch?
